transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-01-28
Start: 16:00 PST
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Lena Park (Redwood AE), Marco Diaz (Redwood SE), Jared Kim (ClearPath Head of ML), Sasha Iyer (ClearPath Platform), Priya Patel (ClearPath Product)

Summary:
Weekly POC sync focused on rollout/go-live planning. Reviewed recent benchmark results, discussed canary strategy (traffic ramp, monitoring, rollback), cutover runbook items, roles & responsibilities, and next steps for final pre-go checklist. Decision to run a phased canary 10% -> 50% -> full over 48 hours with automated alerts and manual rollback gating.

Topics:
- Benchmark results and tuning (batching, kv cache, quantization tradeoffs)
- Canary vs A/B approach and traffic shifting plan
- Monitoring/alerting + runbook (what to watch, who to call)
- Rollback criteria and fallback to hosted model
- Timeline and owners for cutover items

Transcript:
[00:00] Lena: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — I think we have about 45 minutes, agenda is rollouts, canary, runbooks. Marco and I will run through the benchmark highlights and proposed cutover plan, then we'll capture owners.
[00:35] Jared: Sounds good, short on time but want to make sure SLAs and rollback are clear, last week's peak showed a few p95 spikes we need addressed.
[01:12] Marco: Yeah, so quick context — we ran the dedicated pool with the batching config we discussed, KV cache on, int8 quantization. Average latency dropped ~22% and cost per token was about 0.7x relative to hosted baseline. But you saw p95 remained around 420ms during a burst test. There's some tail latency behavior tied to re-batching under heavy concurrency.
[02:05] Sasha: Right, those p95s are the thing. Our product team said 300ms p95 target for API endpoints. Anything we can tune server-side without affecting quality?
[02:45] Marco: We can lower batch window slightly to reduce tail — that'll increase per-token compute but might get p95 into target. Also we can enable a smaller KV cache TTL to avoid cold cache penalties when traffic shifts. There's a tradeoff with cost.
[03:30] Priya: Question — if we change batching, do we need a model re-compile or is it config only?
[03:55] Marco: Mostly config — no model rebuild, but in some configs the runtime picks different kernels which slightly changes perf. We should benchmark the exact config in a short 1-hour run against prod-like traffic.
[04:20] Lena: Action item then: Marco runs a 1-hour benchmark with the lowered batching window and shares logs. Jared, Sasha, you'll get the link.
[04:45] Jared: Yep, please include the traces — we want to see correlation between KV cache misses and p95 spikes.
[05:10] Marco: Will do.
[05:25] Lena: Okay next — canary strategy. Proposed approach: start with 10% traffic for 6 hours, monitor key health metrics and error rates, if stable move to 50% for 12 hours, then 100% after sign-off. If any critical alerts fire, we pause and either rollback or shift to hosted fallback. Thoughts?
[05:52] Sasha: 6 hours feels short for some of our overnight batch traffic, can we make the initial window 12 hours?
[06:20] Jared: Agreed, 12 for the first step, and we should schedule the canary start to avoid our nightly loads, maybe start mid-day PST.
[06:45] Priya: Also A/B could help test quality differences if we change quantization, but adds complexity for product metrics. I'd prefer canary unless we need to compare quality signals.
[07:15] Marco: For quantization changes, we recommend an A/B on a subset of traffic that validates output quality against anchors — but for the initial go-live keep the same model weights and quantization we used in the POC unless you want quality tests.
[07:47] Lena: Noted. Decision leaning to pure canary for rollout, separate A/B for quantization if needed post-go-live.
[08:05] Lena: Now monitoring — what dashboards and alerts do you need? We propose the following as baseline: 5xx rate, p50/p95/p99 latencies, token consumption, error class breakdown, KV cache hit rate, and model quality regression (via sample evals). We'll push Grafana links and Alertmanager rules.
[08:45] Sasha: We need SLO-based alerts: p95 > 350ms for 10 minutes triggers P1 oncall, 5xx rate > 0.5% triggers pager. Also include CPU/GPU saturation metrics.
[09:12] Marco: We'll publish a monitoring doc with exact thresholds. We'll also add a synthetic test hitting typical prompts every minute to detect regressions quickly.
[09:40] Jared: Synthetic tests are huge, please include content anchored on our top 20 prompts.
[10:05] Lena: We'll need runbook steps: how to pause traffic, how to rollback to hosted fallback, who to call, escalation path, and post-mortem owners. Marco, can you include the exact commands to shift traffic?
[10:30] Marco: Yes — in Redwood console it's a route swap with a single toggle for the canary target, plus an API call to modify routing weight. We'll document the CLI/API steps and the console screenshots.
[11:00] Priya: Who owns the final decision to roll back? Product or SRE?
[11:20] Jared: We'll own the go/no-go in product after seeding the SRE input; hotline will be SRE lead + product manager.
[11:40] Lena: Good, capture that in runbook. We'll add explicit gating checklist: no critical alerts for 12 hours, p95 within threshold, token costs within expected band, and no quality regressions in synthetic evals.
[12:05] Marco: On rollback options: we have two paths. Fast rollback — flip route to hosted Redwood model (zero deploy rollback). Full rollback — redeploy previous dedicated config. Fast rollback is immediate but increases cost; we'll prioritize that for availability events.
[12:40] Sasha: Fine. For compliance we need audit logs of each route change and operator identity. Do you capture that?
[12:55] Marco: Yes, Redwood records audit logs with operator and timestamp; we can forward to your SIEM or give read-only access. We'll include link to the audit log export doc.
[13:20] Priya: Also need encryption key details for the private cluster — KMS rotations etc.
[13:35] Lena: That'll be in the security packet we shared earlier — escalate if you need HSM details.
[13:50] Jared: Back on monitoring — what about auto-scaling? If we ramp to 50% traffic will the dedicated pool scale automatically or do we pre-warm?
[14:12] Marco: You have two options: pre-warm a larger pool to guarantee headroom, or configure autoscaling with a short cooldown and burst buffer. For canary we recommend pre-warm for initial ramp to avoid cold starts impacting p95. Post-canary you can rely on autoscale.
[14:40] Lena: So next step: decide on pre-warm size. Marco, can you propose a minimal pre-warm config that keeps p95 < 350ms under expected canary load?
[15:05] Marco: I'll run a sizing estimate and include it in the benchmark output.
[15:20] Sasha: Also, what's the plan for endpoints behind our API gateway? Traffic split must be transparent to our gateway logs.
[15:40] Marco: We'll provide the canary target endpoints; you can route via header-based weight or percent. We'll document required header to opt-in for A/B as well.
[16:05] Lena: Okay, let's talk guardrails and rollback criteria specifics — list them out.
[16:25] Jared: 1) p95 > 400ms sustained for 5 minutes -> pause and investigate. 2) 5xx > 0.5% for 10 minutes -> immediate rollback to hosted. 3) Quality regression above delta threshold on synthetic tests -> pause and run manual evals.
[16:55] Marco: We'll map those to Alertmanager playbooks and include run commands for rollback.
[17:20] Priya: Communication plan during rollback — we need a Slack channel and an incident lead.
[17:35] Lena: We'll create a dedicated #clearpath-redwood-canary channel and add the SRE oncall and product leads.
[17:50] Sasha: Perfect.
[18:05] Lena: Timing — target for canary start is Feb 3rd mid-day PST. We need the final success criteria doc and sign-off by Feb 2nd.
[18:28] Jared: OK we'll aim for Feb 2nd, I'll circulate the doc today and update by next Thursday.
[18:45] Marco: Quick note on metrics collection — include model runtime traces so we can correlate latency spikes to kernel selection or IO waits. That will help root cause if p95 spikes.
[19:05] Jared: Yes please.
[19:20] Lena: Any blocker for go/no-go?
[19:35] Sasha: We need the benchmark with the lowered batching window, and confirmation of monitoring thresholds wired into our pager.
[19:50] Marco: Benchmarks scheduled for tomorrow, will upload to the shared folder and notify.
[20:10] Lena: Great. Let's recap owners and due dates.
[20:25] Lena: Marco: run 1-hour bench w/ lower batching - due 2025-01-31.
[20:35] Marco: Confirmed.
[20:40] Lena: Lena: share cutover runbook draft and rollback playbook - due 2025-02-03.
[20:50] Lena: Confirmed.
[20:55] Jared: Jared: produce final success criteria doc w/ p95, error budget, product sign-off - due 2025-02-05.
[21:05] Jared: I'll get that out.
[21:10] Sasha: Sasha: confirm monitoring access/alerts wired to pager - due 2025-01-30.
[21:22] Sasha: Yep.
[21:30] Priya: Priya: coordinate communication and post-mortem owner - will do.
[21:40] Priya: Ok.
[21:55] Lena: Any other questions?
[22:10] Jared: On rollback we also want a contingency to degrade model to a smaller context window if throughput issues arise, is that supported?
[22:30] Marco: We can serve a lower-context variant, but that's a model artifact — we'd need to test for quality impact. It's doable as an additional fallback path but won't be immediate out-of-the-box.
[22:55] Jared: Fine, add as optional plan B.
[23:10] Lena: Alright, we'll capture that in the runbook as optional fallback.
[23:25] Marco: I'll also include the exact console steps and the API snippet to flip weights, plus an example of the monitoring dashboard panels.
[23:45] Lena: Great — last housekeeping, we'll send the calendar invite for the Feb 3rd canary window and include a 2-hour standby for immediate rollbacks.
[24:00] Jared: Thanks everyone.
[24:15] Lena: Thanks — we'll follow up with the artifacts.
